scope: All 86 generated mutations in daily_schedule, sitting_is_close and continuation_ready, within two modules; results concern the explicitly selected tests, not the complete project or every function in those modules.

budget.timing_excludes: Installation, initial one-mutant smoke and human adjudication.

new_contracts: Unassessed, important and urgent events bypass the daily queue.
Warsaw release instants remain correct on UTC and Asia/Tokyo hosts, before and after the release hour.
Sitting urgency includes its deadline boundary on the Warsaw date.
Only a sent parent with a confirmed message ID unlocks a child.
Missing parents do not borrow the first publication, and saved reply targets remain frozen.
The returned continuation matches its persisted parent binding; a stale queued snapshot cannot overwrite a pending part.

lexinform.services.message_parts.x_conti.reason: Only weakens the assertion that repository callers supply a stored publication and a delivery plan. No invalid-input test was added solely to kill it.

lexinform.delivery_schedule.x_daily_sche.reason: At exactly the release hour the original chooses the next day and the mutant releases immediately. This is behaviorally different; no policy was invented to improve the score.
Converting the detection instant to the host fixed offset before adding 24 hours preserves elapsed time. ISO offset rendering may differ; this is not whole-program textual equivalence.
Timezone conversion preserves the instant used by min and due comparisons. ISO offset rendering may differ; exact operator formatting is outside this pilot contract.

adjudication_probes.equivalence_scope: Scheduling instants, not exact operator ISO timestamp rendering. Finite probes support the algebraic fixed-offset argument; not a whole-program equivalence proof.
adjudication_probes.boundary_policy: Current code chooses the next day; the mutant releases immediately. No new product policy or test asserting either choice was introduced.

reproduction.note: Use the explicit function patterns; bare mutmut run also includes generated functions outside this pilot. Compare survivor classifications, not a project-wide mutation score.

limitations: Selected-scope survivors were not run against every existing test before strengthening the targeted contracts.
Mutmut exit code 1 establishes a failing test run, not which assertion killed each mutation. No timeouts, internal-error exit codes or missing-test results were counted as kills.
No mutation score threshold was added to normal CI.
Continuation snapshotting, freeze_parts, send_continuations and explicit checkpoint reordering mutations remain outside this pilot.
The exact-release boundary remains an open policy case; four remaining survivors were not suppressed.
source_provenance_note: The initial selected run preceded integration of upstream delivery-contract matrices. The second run included that integration; neither target module nor the two original selected scenario files changed, and the upstream matrix tests were outside both selections.

main_integration.coverage_shard_regression: Before the .coverage.* ignore rule, generated worker files flipped source provenance to dirty. The isolated Git regression now ignores shards while detecting a tracked source edit.
